back: The power of an atom to attract the pair of electrons in a covalent bond towards itself.
Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
Electrostatic attraction between a lattice of positive ions and delocalised electrons.
Increases across a period (higher nuclear charge, smaller radius); decreases down a group (larger radius, more shielding). F is highest (4.0).

front: Using electronegativity difference to predict bonding?
back: 0 → non-polar covalent; moderate → polar covalent; large (about 2 or more, metal + non-metal) → mainly ionic.
Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice and carry charge.

front: Why are metals malleable and ductile?
back: Layers of positive ions slide over each other; the delocalised electrons keep attracting them, so the lattice does not break.
More delocalised electrons per atom and smaller, more highly charged ions (Na < Mg < Al).

front: Describe the dot-and-cross diagram of MgO.
back: [Mg]²⁺ and [O]²⁻ in square brackets; the oxide ion has 8 outer electrons: 6 dots + 2 crosses.
